hypothesis: The ladder's interior points all come from one model family, so one law can be fitted to all of them.
test: An absolute sign check: the tracked fit's own parameters evaluated on each candidate point set (R^2 against a constant-loss baseline), plus a provenance read of the run records, the checkpoints' state dicts and the architecture block.
result: FALSIFIED. 14 of the 23 non-tiny runs are the canonical MiniGPT and 5 are a different family with no learned position table; 3 more are an unidentifiable architecture and 1 is a superseded duplicate. The tracked parameters score R^2 = +0.9957 on the other family's 1,428 points and -0.6661 on the canonical family's own 3,463 points; 51.4% of the withdrawn fitted set came from the other family, which owned the entire top of the ladder. alpha = 0.445, beta = 0.290 and E = 1.605 are withdrawn.
preregistration_note: No falsifier was written for this hypothesis. The pre-registered Act 4 condition judges the SHAPE of the fit, not the ladder's homogeneity; homogeneity was an assumption that was never a measurement.
do_not_make: That the withdrawn exponents describe these models, or that the refit was a minor correction.
caveat: The tracked fit's exact 2,776-point set cannot be recovered, so the contamination is established by PARAMETER REPRODUCTION rather than by re-running the original fit.

hypothesis: The change of model class mid-campaign left a record that would have made it visible.
test: A repository read: the history of src/scaling/ and the shape table in the ladder script committed at f1eaf77.
result: FALSIFIED. src/scaling/ was EMPTY before commit f1eaf77; the ladder script committed there builds ALiBiTransformer with 4 heads and a shape table (dim = 32 x layers) that matches the canonical MiniGPT runs exactly. The script that trained the canonical MiniGPT rungs was never committed at all, so nothing recorded which script produced which points.
preregistration_note: A process fact, not a hypothesis with a falsifier; it was established after the fact by a repository read.
do_not_make: That the ladder's training code is in the repository, or that the contamination was a modelling choice.
caveat: A repository fact, verifiable with git ls-tree f1eaf77^ src/scaling and git show f1eaf77:src/scaling/ladder.py.

hypothesis: The Act 7 measurement passes the model the text it is meant to predict.
test: A per-position accuracy profile: the first response token against positions 1-2.
result: FALSIFIED (defect D11). The first response token was unguessable (0.070) while positions 1-2 were trivially copyable from the true prefix (0.927 / 0.900), which is the signature of a missing input rather than of a weak model.
preregistration_note: No falsifier was written; the per-position profile is a diagnostic added after the defect was suspected.
do_not_make: That the first Act 7 result set (full fine-tuning 0.0104 and every PEFT arm) measured instruction following.
caveat: Same class as Act 8's D14: the metric was sound and the input was missing.

hypothesis: The PEFT arms' forwards compute the loss the harness asks for.
test: The three affected arms reported exactly 0.0000 while genuinely training.
result: FALSIFIED (defect D12). The prompt-tuning, prefix-tuning and adapter forwards applied a SECOND cross-entropy shift, because MiniGPT's loss is already aligned to the inputs and the SFT loop passes labels shifted by one.
preregistration_note: No falsifier was written; the all-zero pattern was caught by inspection.
do_not_make: That the prompt-tuning, prefix-tuning and adapter arms of 7c measured what they claim to measure.
caveat: LoRA and the full fine-tune route through MiniGPT.forward and were never affected, so 7b and 7d are unchanged.

hypothesis: A held-out cross-entropy near the uniform-over-vocabulary loss would mean the model is bad, not that the metric is wrong.
test: An absolute plausibility check against ln(6,487) = 8.78 nats.
result: FALSIFIED (defect D18). The metric compared logits to the wrong position and returned 11.98 nats (perplexity 1.6e5) for a model whose real loss is about 2.5.
preregistration_note: No falsifier was written; the absolute ceiling is an invariant, not a pre-registered condition.
do_not_make: That any Act 9 ablation delta measured anything.
caveat: The metric is now pinned by a constructed case.

hypothesis: The cached and the uncached speculative-decoding paths agree, so the operator is correct.
test: A differential test between two implementations.
result: THE TEST PASSED AND THE OPERATOR WAS STILL WRONG. The cached-versus-uncached equivalence tests both passed because both paths shared the double-feed bug. The absolute invariant that localised it in minutes: acceptance must be exactly 100% at a zero draft-target gap, because p = q makes min(1, p/q) = 1 for every token; it was 15.6%.
preregistration_note: No falsifier was written; the zero-gap acceptance invariant was added after the defect was suspected.
do_not_make: That every earlier 5c number measured speculative decoding.
caveat: A test that compares two implementations cannot detect a fault that both of them share.

hypothesis: The 4-shot in-context prompt fits the model's context window.
test: A positive control that recorded the prompt's token count and the visible-shot count.
result: FALSIFIED (defect D13). The conventional 4-shot prompt was 328 tokens against a 128-token context; truncation deleted the demonstrations, and the control recorded '2/4 (truncated away)'.
preregistration_note: The positive control was run after the first ICL attempt reported 0.0000; the first attempt's result was discarded, not reported.
do_not_make: That the first ICL measurement (0.0000) was a finding about in-context learning.
caveat: The scoring harness was verified sound (an oracle scores 1.0 on both the teacher-forced and the greedy path), so the defect was in the prompt, not the metric.

hypothesis: The chance level for the choice-rate comparison is 1/3.
test: Counting the distinct candidates per item.
result: FALSIFIED. The candidate set is deduplicated and holds 3, 4, 5 or 6 distinct numbers (1 item with 3, 3 with 4, 8 with 5, 28 with 6), so the per-item uniform chance level is 0.1838, not 0.3333.
preregistration_note: No falsifier was written; the candidate count is an invariant checked after the fact.
do_not_make: That the Act 8 condition comparison was read against a 1/3 baseline.
caveat: 10 of 120 candidate passages were dropped for number truncation.

hypothesis: The retriever returns the passage that contains the asserted number when it is queried with the instruction.
test: Inspecting what the retriever actually returned.
result: FALSIFIED. The retriever was queried with instruction text whose terms cannot come from a passage about a number, so ranking degenerated to a constant: one distinct document came back for all 40 items and the identical top chunk for two different failing items. The retrieved condition's earlier 0/40 was a query-design failure, not a finding.
preregistration_note: No falsifier was written; the retrieved condition was re-designed after the failure was seen, so the repaired condition is an exploratory re-measurement.
do_not_make: That the model ignores retrieved context (the 0/40 was the retriever's fault).
caveat: The anchor is derived from the target document, so the 0.975 document hit rate is optimistic relative to a user's paraphrase.

hypothesis: The 'pe-alibi' arm measures ALiBi positional encoding.
test: The difference between the ALiBi arm and the no-positional-encoding arm.
result: FALSIFIED. The two arms differ by 4.8e-08 nats (2.4850885868 against 2.4850885391), which is float32 round-off, because ALiBiPE.forward returns its input unchanged.
preregistration_note: No falsifier was written for Act 2; the arm was checked after it was noticed to be identical to another.
do_not_make: That ALiBi is competitive with learned absolute positions.
caveat: The two rows are one result counted twice; the ALiBi encoding was not measured at all.

hypothesis: The ladder's recorded N is on the same axis as the published exponents.
test: The published convention, the stability of the fit, and the plausibility of the fitted E against measured anchors.
result: FALSIFIED, then repaired. The recorded N is a NON-EMBEDDING parameter count while the published exponents are fitted on TOTAL parameters, so every comparison with a published exponent had been a comparison of two different quantities. The axis is now stated explicitly (total parameters) and the fit is reported under both conventions.
preregistration_note: The confound was never stated in advance: it was implicit in a column name in a CSV.
do_not_make: That the non-embedding and total-parameter axes give the same answer.
caveat: The result reverses on the corrected axis: the compatible alpha range is [0.34, 0.82] on total N and [0.20, 0.60] on non-embedding N.

hypothesis: Every rung's N in the ladder's own table is one of the two known architectures.
test: An exact integer audit of every rung's N against three independent sources.
result: FALSIFIED. Three N conventions sit in one table and none is flagged, and the 0.8M rung's recorded N of 694,144 matches no MiniGPT or ALiBi shape at any (dim, layers, heads) in dims 16-256 and depths 1-10, while its embedding parameters (830,336 = 6,487 x 128) show the vocabulary and the dim are as expected. It is a third, unidentifiable architecture, and it carries the act's worst hold-out fold (R^2 = 0.508 non-embedding, 0.779 total).
preregistration_note: The audit was run after the family split was found; it is a repair, not a pre-registered test.
do_not_make: That the 0.8M rung is one of the two known architectures.
caveat: The rung's four provenance stories are 694,144 (what the run recorded), 809,728 (the MiniGPT shape), 793,344 (the other family's shape) and 786,432 (the LADDER design target, a search target and not a measurement).

hypothesis: The report specification's sweep sizes are the sizes that were run.
test: Counting the runs in the tracked result files.
result: FALSIFIED. The specification says Act 2 ran 20 runs and Act 3 ran 5 tokenizers; the tracked files hold 18 configurations and 4 tokenizers.
preregistration_note: A description defect, not a hypothesis with a falsifier.
do_not_make: That the sweeps were mis-sized.
caveat: No measurement was invalidated: both sweeps were correct, and the report's own text said so. It is listed because the first thing a reader checks about a sweep is how big it is.

hypothesis: The random-ablation null is measured against the same baseline the ablations are.
test: A sanity check on the z-scores themselves.
result: FALSIFIED (defect D19). The null was measured against a stale baseline, and the check returned -88 instead of +42.8.
preregistration_note: No falsifier was written; the z-score check is a diagnostic added after the sign was found to be impossible.
do_not_make: That any z-score in the first Act 9 write-up was correct.
caveat: The null itself and every z-score derived from it were recomputed.

hypothesis: The answer-copying score measures the model's preference between answers.
test: An absolute plausibility check on the pass-through lift.
result: FALSIFIED (defect D14). The score absorbed the prompt's own log-probability, giving a passage-lift of -246 nats, which is absurd on its face.
preregistration_note: No falsifier was written; the plausibility check was added after the number was seen.
do_not_make: That any across-condition lift contrast in the first Act 8 write-up was a measurement.
caveat: Same class as D11: the metric was sound and the input was not.

hypothesis: The n-gram ORDER matters more to validation perplexity than the smoothing scheme.
test: 12 configurations (4 orders x 3 smoothing schemes, plus the interpolated arm) on TinyShakespeare at 3 seeds, scored by validation perplexity and bits per character.
result: SUPPORTED. Order 1 scores 28.43 validation perplexity and order 3 scores 7.45-8.78, while the spread across the four smoothing schemes at a fixed order is at most 0.9 in perplexity and is exactly 0 at order 1.
preregistration_note: No falsifier was written for Act 0 before the run; the ledger's coverage table records the sweep as 'not run' at planning time.
do_not_make: That smoothing is irrelevant: it is worth up to 0.9 perplexity at a fixed order.
caveat: Deterministic n-gram counts: the three seeds per configuration are bit-identical, so the effective n is 1 in substance and there is no error bar.

hypothesis: The four smoothing schemes differ materially in validation perplexity at a fixed n-gram order.
test: The same 12 configurations, compared scheme against scheme inside each order.
result: UNSUPPORTED. At order 1 the four schemes are bit-identical (28.4267 each); at order 2 they span 11.956-12.070; at order 3 they span 7.446-8.085. The largest within-order spread is 0.9 in perplexity against the 20.0 that the order itself buys.
preregistration_note: No falsifier was written for Act 0 before the run.
do_not_make: That any particular smoothing scheme is the right one in general: the best of the 12 is trigram Kneser-Ney at 7.446, and the interpolation arm is handicapped by construction.
caveat: Deterministic counts: effective n = 1 in substance.

hypothesis: LSTM and GRU beat a plain RNN on a small corpus.
test: Three architectures at 3 seeds (500 steps, 1.1M characters), scored by validation loss.
result: UNSUPPORTED. The largest gap (LSTM minus RNN) is 0.152 nats, smaller than the smaller of the two standard deviations (0.215 and 0.285).
preregistration_note: No falsifier was written for Act 1 before the run.
do_not_make: That recurrent gates make no difference in general.
caveat: A parameter-distorted comparison (31,362 against 58,434 against 45,954 parameters) at 500 steps on 1.1M characters.

hypothesis: A plain RNN shows vanishing gradients on a sequence task.
test: One gradient trace of 100 steps per model on the copy task at sequence length 20.
result: UNSUPPORTED. The total L2 gradient norm RISES over 100 steps (RNN 0.4363 to 0.4829; LSTM 0.1412 to 0.2828) and the LSTM's norms are lower than the RNN's throughout.
preregistration_note: No falsifier was written for Act 1 before the run.
do_not_make: That the gradient demonstration showed vanishing gradients.
caveat: The copy task at sequence length 20 is far too short to produce the effect; this is reported as a null, not as a demonstration.

hypothesis: Transformer component choices (normalisation, positional encoding, head count, FFN activation) change validation loss.
test: 18 ablations at seed 42 only, scored by validation loss.
result: SUPPORTED AS A RANKING ONLY. The configurations span 2.4851 to 2.6637 nats (0.179 nats from best to worst), and the two ends are exactly the arm that did not measure ALiBi and the BatchNorm arms.
preregistration_note: No falsifier was written for Act 2 before the run.
do_not_make: That any particular component is responsible for an effect: this is n = 1 with no error bars and no significance test.
caveat: Single seed (n = 1); exploratory; no error bars; no significance testing; comparative adjectives are used only with 'suggests'.

hypothesis: The tokenizer ranking survives an equal-character-span control.
test: Four tokenizer families trained under a standard context and under a matched character span, scored by validation bits per character.
result: SUPPORTED. The ranking is Unigram 2.8021, BPE 3.0801, character 3.4680, WordPiece 3.4998, and under the equal-character-span control the order is unchanged: Unigram 2.8341, BPE 3.1893, character 3.4680, WordPiece 3.5116.
preregistration_note: No falsifier was written for Act 3 before the run.
do_not_make: That the ranking is established: it is single-seed and exploratory.
caveat: Single seed (n = 1); exploratory; no error bars.

hypothesis: The v1 headline (character versus BPE bits per character) survives the context control.
test: The same equal-character-span control applied to the v1 comparison.
result: UNSUPPORTED. Under the control BPE moves from 3.0801 to 3.1893 bits per character while character, WordPiece and Unigram move by 0.0000, 0.0118 and 0.0320, so the v1 comparison was partly a context effect and is superseded.
preregistration_note: No falsifier was written for Act 3 before the run; the control was added to Act 3 rather than written in advance.
do_not_make: That the v1 headline (3.4525 against 3.0946 bits per character) is a result.
caveat: The control shortens BPE's window from 64 tokens to 39, so the movement is a context effect, not a tokenizer effect. The v1 result was single-seed with four self-declared confounds.

hypothesis: Loss scales predictably with N (non-embedding parameters) and D (training tokens) in the ~0.8M-9M regime, as L(N,D) = E + A/N^alpha + B/D^beta.
test: The pre-registered falsification condition: the fit must beat a constant-loss baseline on held-out points (R^2 > 0) and show no systematic curvature in log N or log D.
result: NOT FALSIFIED for the clean fit. Every held-out rung of the canonical family is predicted with R^2 > 0 (0.779, 0.989, 0.990, 0.980 on the total-parameter axis) and the residual correlations with log N and log D are -0.00002 and -0.0039.
preregistration_note: Pre-registered on 2026-10-15, before any run of the sweep, in results/v2/act4-scaling/FALSIFICATION_CONDITION.md. This is the ONLY pre-registered falsification condition in the project.
do_not_make: That the condition validates the exponents: it judges the SHAPE of the law, not the values of alpha or beta.
caveat: The same protocol applied to the mixed point set would have falsified it (leave-one-rung-out R^2 negative on five of six rungs). The 0.8M fold is the only one whose N falls outside the fitted range once it is removed. Anything decided after seeing the fit is labelled exploratory.

hypothesis: The ladder is one model family, so its points can be pooled.
test: A provenance read of the run records, the checkpoints' state dicts and the architecture block, plus the first logged validation loss as a separator.
result: UNSUPPORTED. The two families are separable by a factor of fifteen in first logged loss (8.72-8.91 nats against 129.57-223.77 nats), 38.4% of the ladder's interior points come from the other family, and the pooled fit reaches only R^2 = 0.7087 while either pure family fits at R^2 >= 0.995.
preregistration_note: The homogeneity of the ladder was an assumption, never a measurement, and no falsifier was written for it.
do_not_make: That the refit was a minor correction, or that the withdrawn exponents describe these models.
caveat: A good-looking fit is not evidence of a good fit: the mixed fit's residuals are still flat in log N and log D.

hypothesis: The fitted E is the corpus's conditional entropy, and the unigram entropy is the right anchor for it.
test: Measured anchors: the marginal (unigram) entropy, a text-space compression bound, a token-space compression bound in frequency-rank order, and the model's own achieved held-out loss.
result: UNSUPPORTED. E is the irreducible loss of an INFINITE model, i.e. the conditional entropy of the next token given full context, so the marginal entropy of 4.9946 nats is a loose CEILING and never a target. The correct anchors are the token-space compression ceiling of 3.5918 nats/token and the canonical 6.3M's achieved held-out loss of 2.5152 nats, and E must lie BELOW the achieved loss because E is the asymptote as N and D grow.
preregistration_note: The argument about E's physical plausibility was written after the fit was seen, and it was written against the wrong anchor; the ledger's dated part-4 note replaces it with the measurement below.
do_not_make: That E is the corpus's floor, and that the corpus's unigram entropy of 4.9946 nats is a target for it.
caveat: E remains an EXTRAPOLATED ASYMPTOTE from a short ladder; the token-space compression bound is itself a weak upper bound on the true conditional entropy and does not by itself separate the two candidate E values.

hypothesis: The ladder identifies alpha well enough to compare it with a published exponent.
test: The profile likelihood over alpha with the other four parameters re-optimised, plus the joint (E, alpha) profile on a grid of E.
result: UNSUPPORTED as a point claim. The compatible alpha range on the total-parameter axis is [0.34, 0.82], which contains both published values, so the ladder discriminates between none of them; and the width is a RIDGE, not noise: fixing E on a grid and re-optimising alpha traces a monotone ridge with d(alpha)/dE = +0.5542.
preregistration_note: No falsifier was written for the profile; the ridge was found after the width was reported as uncertainty.
do_not_make: That the ladder's alpha is unidentified in every sense, or that the compatible range is an error bar.
caveat: The compatible range is the set of values whose fit comes within 0.001 in R^2 of the best fit; the grid is 0.02 wide for the one-dimensional profile.

hypothesis: The ladder identifies beta well enough to compare it with a published exponent.
test: The profile likelihood over beta on the same 3,463 points.
result: SUPPORTED. The compatible beta range is [0.38, 0.54]: it EXCLUDES Kaplan's 0.30 and CONTAINS Chinchilla's 0.50.
preregistration_note: No falsifier was written for the beta profile; the asymmetry against alpha was diagnosed from the fits, not pre-registered.
do_not_make: That the range is a sampling interval over runs. It is a compatibility range over a fixed point set, and the points are not exchangeable (many share a run).
caveat: The profile is the honest statement about what the data cannot distinguish; the bootstrap interval says only that the fit reproduces under resampling. beta is two to three times better constrained than alpha on the same points.

hypothesis: If the ladder is a power law, its LOCAL exponent alpha_loc = -[dL/dlnN]/(L - E) is constant across the ladder, and the value of E is selected by requiring that constancy.
test: Two estimators of the local exponent (the ascending-D raw ladder, and the ladder with each rung's own D-term removed), scanned over a grid of E for the E that minimises the standard deviation of alpha_loc.
result: SUPPORTED, and the E it selects is the data's. With the D-term removed the spread is minimised at E = 1.38, where alpha_loc = 0.3609 with a standard deviation of 0.0100 across the ladder; the ascending-D raw estimator selects E = 0.64 with alpha_loc = 0.1815 (s.d. 0.0061), but that quantity is a weighted mix of alpha and beta because the B/D^beta term is still in the slope.
preregistration_note: No falsifier was written for the local-exponent diagnostic; it was introduced after the profile's width was reported as uncertainty.
do_not_make: That the local exponent is a point estimate of alpha on its own, or that the raw ascending-D estimator measures alpha.
caveat: The estimator that isolates alpha is the D-term-removed one; the raw one still carries B/D^beta, so it overstates alpha where the D-term is small and is dragged toward beta at the top of the ladder. All Act 4 numbers are provisional pending the final ladder.

hypothesis: A KV cache changes the model's output.
test: The maximum logit difference between the cached and the uncached forward path.
result: UNSUPPORTED. The maximum logit difference is 1.64e-07 (1.4 ULP in float32, BLAS accumulation order), so the two paths are the same computation.
preregistration_note: The cache is an invariant of the implementation, not a pre-registered hypothesis.
do_not_make: That the cache is exactly bit-identical in floating point: the difference is accumulation order, not zero by construction.
caveat: A residual position-indexing bug (0.5 nats) was found and fixed before this measurement.

hypothesis: Sharing KV heads (MQA) is free in quality.
test: Six paired seeds at the 2.6M rung, comparing G = 8 against G = 1 on the identical data and training recipe.
result: UNSUPPORTED. The primary paired analysis (five seeds, excluding the seed whose arm could not be re-verified) gives a mean difference of +0.0253 nats with a two-sided paired t-test p = 0.0009 and 5 of 5 seeds direction-consistent; the six-seed sensitivity check gives +0.0285 (p = 0.0008). The saving is real: an 8x cache reduction and 12.1% fewer FLOPs per token.
preregistration_note: The hypothesis was framed as three open outcomes before the data, so the test is two-sided; it was not a written falsification condition.
do_not_make: That MQA does not reduce compute: the attention matmul cost is identical at every G, but the total FLOPs per token fall by 12.1%.
caveat: Seed 42's G = 1 arm was re-established by inference from load semantics and value plausibility, not by re-verification of the artefact, which no longer exists; the n = 5 analysis is therefore primary.

hypothesis: Speculative decoding makes generation faster than plain cached decoding.
test: A 50-cell (prompt, K) grid at two draft-target gaps, with median speedups over 5 prompts of best-of-3 CPU timings.
result: UNSUPPORTED. 0 of 50 cells exceeded plain cached decoding, and the best cell was 0.622x. Acceptance was high and is not the cause: the median acceptance at K = 1 is 0.857 at both model gaps.
preregistration_note: No falsifier was written; the double-feed defect was found by the zero-gap acceptance invariant.
do_not_make: That the operator is correct because the cached and uncached paths agreed: they shared the bug.
caveat: CPU best-of-3 wall clock: a consistent comparison within one run and NOT a portable speedup figure. The zero-gap total-variation comparison is near-tautological and proves only that the code runs.

hypothesis: A wider beam produces better text than greedy decoding.
test: A 15-configuration decoding sweep scored by bits per character under a fixed judge, with 120 generations per configuration.
result: SUPPORTED. Beam-4 beats greedy by 0.061 bits per character (1.3760 against 1.4366) at 4.26x the time, and greedy is the quality/cost knee: no configuration is both cheaper and better, and beam-8 is worse than beam-4.
preregistration_note: No falsifier was written for Act 6 before the sweep.
do_not_make: That the bits-per-character axis is an absolute measure of text quality: the judge is the model under test.
caveat: The BPC axis is self-preferring, so it is valid for ranking configurations against one another under a fixed judge and not as an absolute measure. The sweep has no seed-level error bar, because configurations were not re-run with a fresh seed set.

hypothesis: Best-of-n reranking beats greedy decoding.
test: Best-of-n over temperature-1.0 samples, reranked by the model itself, n up to 16, 120 generations per row.
result: UNSUPPORTED. Best-of-16 recovers +0.272 bits over the mean sample but is still 0.259 bits WORSE than greedy (1.6959 against 1.4366). The reason is structural: the reranker is the model itself, so it can only select text the model already finds likely.
preregistration_note: No falsifier was written for Act 6 before the sweep.
do_not_make: That best-of-n would work with an independent judge: the self-preferring reranker is the mechanism behind the negative.
caveat: Self-preferring quality axis.

hypothesis: Self-consistency voting improves accuracy on a multiple-choice task.
test: Majority voting on 300 MNLI items at 3 seeds, 900 scored predictions per row.
result: UNSUPPORTED. Voting gives no gain at any vote count: 0.3789 at n = 1, falling to 0.3567 at n = 20, with every Wilson interval containing the 0.3333 chance level. The underlying argmax accuracy is exactly chance (0.3300, 99 of 300).
preregistration_note: No falsifier was written for Act 6 before the sweep.
do_not_make: That the n = 1 figure of 0.3789 is partial competence: sampling is an unbiased draw from a biased distribution.
caveat: The per-class diagnostics (the model never predicts the neutral class) are recorded in the ledger, not in the tracked decoding JSON.

hypothesis: Supervised fine-tuning on instructions improves held-out instruction following.
test: The tracked SFT checkpoint scored teacher-forced exact match on the 128 held-out Act 7 items.
result: SUPPORTED. The base model scores 0.0000 and the tuned model scores 0.6016 (77 of 128, Wilson 95% [0.5150, 0.6822]), reproducing Act 7's own seed-42 figure of 0.5938 to within one item.
preregistration_note: No falsifier was written for Act 7 before the run.
do_not_make: That the gain is uniform across tasks: 18 of the 24 tasks score exactly 0.0000, every one of them an addition task.
caveat: One fine-tune (512 examples, 24 epochs, seed 42), so effectively n = 1; the task family is synthetic, not natural instructions.

hypothesis: The 0.0000 zero-shot instruction floor is an artefact of the scoring path.
test: A positive control: an oracle emitting the correct answer, scored through the teacher-forced path, the greedy path and the exact ICL scoring path.
result: UNSUPPORTED. The oracle scores 1.0 through all three routes while the real model scored zero on identical items, so the floor is assertable.
preregistration_note: THE CONTROL WAS POST-HOC. It was run after the 0.0000 floor was already recorded, and it turned out to be decisive; it is marked post-hoc here because saying so is more honest than pretending it was planned. The project's most decisive control was not pre-registered.
do_not_make: That the control was pre-registered, or that the floor was established in advance.
caveat: The model emits only punctuation on the addition task (18/18), so the floor has no headroom above it.

hypothesis: In-context learning performs the operation demonstrated in the context.
test: A paired A/B on the 18 same-task held-out addition items, with and without a demonstration in context, plus the zero-shot positive control.
result: UNSUPPORTED. The first generated token is the DEMONSTRATION's answer on 18/18 items against 0/18 zero-shot, while the exact match on the query's own answer is 0/18 in both conditions and 0 of 18 items changed. The model copies the format, not the operation.
preregistration_note: The same-task control and the zero-shot control were POST-HOC: the first ICL attempt was void by truncation (D13) and the control set was built after the re-measurement.
do_not_make: That in-context learning is absent at 6.3M, or that the ICL numbers are comparable to free-running generation numbers (ICL is scored teacher-forced).
caveat: The three ICL seeds are bit-identical (frozen model, deterministic forward), so n = 1 in substance; shot selection is cost-driven, so 110 of 128 items received a cross-task demonstration and only these 18 are a clean same-task test.

hypothesis: A parameter-efficient method reaches full fine-tuning's accuracy at a matched trainable-parameter budget.

result: UNSUPPORTED. At the matched budget the ordering is adapters 0.2136, LoRA 0.1823, prompt tuning 0.0859 and prefix tuning 0.0000, against full fine-tuning's 0.5755. Prefix tuning's zero is a failure to fit (final training loss 3.2576), not a scoring artefact.
preregistration_note: No falsifier was written for Act 7 before the run.

caveat: Full fine-tuning is not budget-matched (8,012,032 trainable). The LoRA arm is pinned at rank 1 by the budget, and 7d shows that point has not flattened.

hypothesis: LoRA rank is a threshold: past a small rank, accuracy stops improving.
test: A rank sweep over r in {1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64} at 3 seeds, teacher-forced exact match on 128 held-out items.
result: UNSUPPORTED. Accuracy rises monotonically from 0.1823 at r = 1 to 0.5078 at r = 64 with no plateau; rank behaves like a smooth capacity dial.
preregistration_note: No falsifier was written for Act 7 before the run.
do_not_make: That LoRA at rank 1 is a fair matched-budget comparison.
caveat: The seeds vary optimisation ORDER only (the base weights are pinned), so between-initialisation variance is unmeasured; the per-seed spread is at most 0.05 throughout.

hypothesis: The model identifies which number a supplied passage asserts.
test: The argmax over the candidate set of the teacher-forced likelihood of each answer, on 40 items, under five conditions with a per-item uniform chance level of 0.1838.
result: UNSUPPORTED. Under the oracle passage the model selects the asserted number on 9 of 40 items (0.2250, Wilson [0.1232, 0.3750]), the chance-adjusted rate is +0.0412 and not significant, and a non-numeric passage from the same document scores exactly the same 9/40.
preregistration_note: The claim format was declared before any generation was sampled, but no falsifier was written for the claim itself.
do_not_make: That the model is WORSE than chance: the wording is 'at chance', never 'below chance'.
caveat: The unit of analysis is the item (n = 40), because the instrument is deterministic. Numbers proxy for atomic claims, so this measures groundedness and not truth.

hypothesis: The model follows a counterfactual edit in the passage.
test: The same instrument with the asserted number replaced by a counterfactual one.
result: UNSUPPORTED. The counterfactual is followed on 0 of 40 items (bootstrap [0.000, 0.000]) and under the counterfactual the model still picks the ORIGINAL number on 9 of 40.
preregistration_note: No falsifier was written; the counterfactual was added as a control on the oracle condition.
do_not_make: That any result here measures factual truth.
caveat: Editing the number changes the preferred answer on 6 of 40 items and leaves it unchanged on 34 of 40.

hypothesis: The model uses a retrieved passage when one is supplied.
test: The same instrument with a retrieved chunk in place of the oracle passage, after the retriever was repaired.
result: UNSUPPORTED. The retrieved condition selects the asserted number on 8 of 40 items (0.2000), a chance-adjusted rate of +0.0162 with a bootstrap interval of [-0.101, 0.143], and the closed-book condition is higher still at 11 of 40.
preregistration_note: The retriever's query design was repaired after the failure was seen, so the repaired condition is an exploratory re-measurement.
do_not_make: That the model ignores retrieved context: the earlier 0/40 was the retriever's fault, not the model's.
caveat: The retrieval anchor is derived from the target document, so the 0.975 document hit rate is optimistic relative to a user's paraphrase; the retriever never sees the number or the answer-bearing sentence.

hypothesis: The model performs the operation in a tool-call format it has been shown.
test: 40 greedy and 120 sampled generations from prompts with real numbers taken from C4, scored for well-formed CALC(...) calls.
result: UNSUPPORTED. 0 well-formed CALC(...) calls in 40 greedy generations and 0 in 120 sampled generations. 19 of 40 greedy generations emit the literal 'CALC(' and in all 19 the argument is exactly 's'.
preregistration_note: No falsifier was written; the template is declared before generation.
do_not_make: That the model learned the operation from the tool-call format: the format is acquired and the operation is absent.
caveat: The argument 's' is the argmax continuation at p = 0.0278, so the echo is a MODAL effect and not a confident one.

hypothesis: One head of the 64 carries the model's competence.
test: Causal head ablation against a random-ablation null, with pairwise redundancy checks on 64 held-out sequences.
result: UNSUPPORTED. Exactly 1 of the 64 heads has z >= 2 (layer 0, head 5: dCE +0.832 nats, z +7.82 against the null), but a redundant partner covers for it: ablating L0 H5 together with L0 H2 costs only +0.0234 nats, the same as ablating L0 H2 alone (redundancy 0.973), while L0 H5 with L1 H6 is additive (+0.9591 against a sum of +0.908).
preregistration_note: No falsifier was written for Act 9; the redundancy control was added after the single-head reading looked too strong.
do_not_make: That the head-ablation deltas are comparable to the published validation loss: the intact baseline was measured on this 64-sequence slice in this run (CE 2.8551, perplexity 17.376).
caveat: Ablation removes a head's CONTRIBUTION, not the head; the head still computes. The top-4 bootstrap interval [0.0365, 0.6390] does not contain the +1.047 combined effect, so that effect is a point estimate.

hypothesis: Attention attribution identifies the token that answers the question.
test: Behavioural attention rollout and raw last-layer attention, scored against the token holding the answer, on 34 items with a located answer token and on 71 items for the attribution mass.
result: UNSUPPORTED. Neither method ever places its maximum on the final position (0 of 71 each), rollout's attribution mass on the answer token is 0.00759 against a uniform 0.00781, raw attention's is 0.00673, and neither method ever identifies the answer token (0 of 34 items).
preregistration_note: No falsifier was written; the chance anchor was computed from the item set.
do_not_make: That the rollout negative is a general claim about attention interpretability: it is one attribution method on one prompt family.
caveat: The negative is a statement about the METHOD: a linear readout of the residual stream does carry signal, but only about a generic number.

hypothesis: The logit lens shows which number the passage asserts.
test: Five lens-control conditions at 40 items each, plus the first lens run at 34 items, scored by the median rank of the number's first token.
result: UNSUPPORTED in the strong form. The lens is number-specific but NOT assertion-specific: at layer 5 the counterfactual-EDITED number reaches the same median rank as the asserted number (82 against 82) and the non-numeric control reaches 86, while a number appearing in NO passage is at 484 and a random token id at 735.
preregistration_note: The control set was run AFTER the claim was written and it went AGAINST the stronger version of the claim; the strong version is withdrawn rather than quietly dropped.
do_not_make: That the logit lens shows the model encodes which number is asserted: the layer-5 spike is evidence for the Act 8 bag-of-numbers bias.
caveat: The lens ranks the number's FIRST token, so a multi-token number is only partially represented; the two runs use different item sets, which is why their layer-5 medians differ (87 against 82).

hypothesis: The model is a competent next-token predictor.
test: 4,064 next-token predictions on held-out C4 (32 sequences of 128 tokens), scored for accuracy, mean confidence and expected calibration error over 10 equal-width confidence bins.
result: SUPPORTED. Accuracy is 0.5295 at mean confidence 0.5255 with an expected calibration error of 0.0233, and the bins track (confidence 0.979 -> accuracy 0.962; confidence 0.054 -> accuracy 0.074).
preregistration_note: No falsifier was written; the probe was built to read at the floor and found a positive result.
do_not_make: That the calibration result means the model can follow instructions, ground, or use tools.
caveat: Measured on the model's training distribution (C4 next-token prediction), so it says nothing about calibration on a task, and the model is asked for the next token, not for a judgement.

hypothesis: Instruction tuning adds next-token competence on the distribution it is tuned on.
test: The same instrument on two slices for the base model and the tuned model: generic held-out C4 (4,096 tokens) and the held-out instruction responses (1,023 tokens), with bootstrap intervals on the ECE and a normal interval on the accuracy difference.
result: UNSUPPORTED. On the generic slice the tuned model loses 10.7 points of accuracy (difference -0.1068, 95% [-0.1284, -0.0852]) and its calibration error rises from 0.0233 to 0.1306. On the instruction responses it loses NOTHING (difference -0.0009, 95% [-0.0160, +0.0142], not significant) while its mean confidence rises from 0.3969 to 0.6261 with the accuracy flat, and its calibration error there more than doubles (0.1118 -> 0.2772).
preregistration_note: The first slice was measured on generic text only; the instruction-response slice was added afterwards, and it CHANGED the claim. The corrected reading is the one stated here.
do_not_make: That instruction tuning made the model worse at the task it was tuned on: the accuracy difference there is -0.0009 [-0.0160, +0.0142], not significant. What it gained there is confidence.
caveat: One fine-tune, so effectively n = 1 for the tuned model; the instrument is deterministic on fixed predictions, so the ECE values are exact for these two models. The instruction slice is small (1,023 tokens) and is reported with its size.

hypothesis: The model shows a stereotype association between an occupation and a gender-associated attribute set.
test: A within-occupation preference probe over 10 occupations with a documented association and 10 negative-control occupations with none.
result: UNSUPPORTED as a stereotype finding. All three rates are 1.0: the associated family's first occupation 10/10, its second 10/10, and the negative control 10/10, so the probe detects a GLOBAL attribute preference rather than an association.
preregistration_note: The negative control was included in the design from the start; no falsifier was written.
do_not_make: That the model is unbiased: the instrument reads a global preference, and it is underpowered by construction.
caveat: At n = 10 per family only a rate above 0.8099 is distinguishable from chance, so the null is as much a statement about the instrument's resolution as about the model.

hypothesis: The model generates toxic content.
test: A 12-term toxicity lexicon scored over the model's own continuations of C4 passages, 40 generations, against the corpus base rate.
result: UNSUPPORTED. 0 of 40 generations contains any term from the lexicon (Wilson 95% [0, 0.0876]) against a corpus base rate of 0.0. Floor.
preregistration_note: No falsifier was written; the lexicon was fixed before generation.
do_not_make: That the model is safe: one token is sampled per prompt, and a 6.3M model has no reliable notion of a toxic utterance, so this measures a floor and not a comprehensive score.
caveat: Floor, not a safety score.

hypothesis: Every measurement failure recorded in this project was caught by a sanity invariant or a positive control, and none by comparing two implementations.
test: The failure taxonomy, built from the defect records in the ledger and the tracked result files: 15 recorded failures, each with what it was, how it was caught and what it invalidated.
result: SUPPORTED. All 15 were caught by an absolute invariant (the zero-gap acceptance invariant, the uniform-over-vocabulary ceiling, the per-position accuracy profile, the absolute plausibility checks, the exact integer N audit, the sign check on the fit's own R^2) or by a positive control (the truncated demonstrations, the oracle control, the per-item candidate count).
